classes.read: Reads only. The MCP server offers its tool by default.
classes.control: Changes a session or a project. The MCP server offers its tool only with --allow control.
classes.answer: Answers an agent's question. The MCP server offers its tool only with --allow answer.
classes.run: Runs a command on the host. The MCP server offers it only with --allow run.
classes.commands: Runs an entry of the owner's command list on the host. The MCP server offers its tool only with --allow commands.
classes.files: Reads and writes files on this Mac and on the host. The MCP server offers its tool only with --allow files, and a copy through it uses only the folders that ~/.config/tokiwa/transfer-dirs lists on this Mac.
classes.human: Needs a person or a terminal: a browser sign-in, hidden input, a root shell or an attached view. Never an MCP tool.

tool.name: tokiwa_sessions
tool.description: List the Tokiwa sessions on the workstation as JSON: name, identity, folder, project, attached clients and pane commands.

tool.name: tokiwa_screen
tool.description: Read the last lines of one Tokiwa session, with its scrollback, as JSON. Take name and identity from tokiwa_sessions. The call refuses a session whose identity changed.

tool.name: tokiwa_search
tool.description: Search the whole scrollback of one Tokiwa session for a text, without regard to case, and return the latest matching lines, each with two lines before and after it, as JSON. Use it to find what a session printed before the last 200 lines. Take name and identity from tokiwa_sessions. The call refuses a session whose identity changed.

tool.name: tokiwa_health
tool.description: Read host and workbench metrics as JSON: CPU, memory, disks, network and service state.

tool.name: tokiwa_status
tool.description: Check AWS access, the host state and the Tokiwa workbench server.

tool.name: tokiwa_digest
tool.description: One line of facts for each Tokiwa session, as JSON: the state that its agent reported and since when, when its screen last changed, and the git state of its folder (branch, unpushed commits, changed files, last commit and its time). Commit messages are not included.

tool.name: tokiwa_state
tool.description: Read the facts of one Tokiwa session as JSON, without screen text: its program, clients, writable clients and driver. Take name and identity from tokiwa_sessions. The call refuses a session whose identity changed.

tool.name: tokiwa_agent_state
tool.description: Read the facts of one Tokiwa session and what the agent in it reports, as JSON: state, turn, pending item and dialog. Call it before tokiwa_agent_wait or tokiwa_agent_send. Take name and identity from tokiwa_sessions. The call refuses a session whose identity changed.

tool.name: tokiwa_agent_wait
tool.description: Wait until the agent of one Tokiwa session ends a turn after the turn count in after, asks for a person, shows a dialog or exits, then return its state with a reason (turn-ended, pending, dialog, ended or timeout). A timeout is a normal result with reason timeout, not an error. Take after from the turn of tokiwa_agent_state, or from turn_before of tokiwa_agent_send.

tool.name: tokiwa_agent_read
tool.description: Read the transcript of the agent of one Tokiwa session in pages, as JSON events. Without tools, a tool call and its result carry no text. Pass the cursor of the last page in after to continue. With pending, read the waiting question or permission request instead. Take name and identity from tokiwa_sessions.

tools.name: tokiwa_create
tools.description: Create a Tokiwa session in its own folder, named after it, inside a project's folder. Take dir from the projects of tokiwa_sessions. The session starts with a shell.

tools.name: tokiwa_launch
tools.description: Create a Tokiwa session in its own folder and type one command line into its shell, for example an agent with its first message. The command runs on the host as the workbench user.

tool.name: tokiwa_interrupt
tool.description: Send Esc to one Tokiwa session, which stops the current turn of Claude Code or Codex. Take name and identity from tokiwa_sessions. The call refuses a session whose identity changed.

tool.name: tokiwa_freeze
tool.description: Pause every process of one Tokiwa session until tokiwa_resume. A model request in progress can be lost; files and the conversation stay. Take name and identity from tokiwa_sessions. The call refuses a session whose identity changed.

tool.name: tokiwa_resume
tool.description: Continue a Tokiwa session that tokiwa_freeze paused. Take name and identity from tokiwa_sessions.

tool.name: tokiwa_agent_send
tool.description: Send one message to the idle agent of one Tokiwa session, as one paste and Enter. The MCP tool passes the message with --text, so the text is in the process arguments of the launcher on the Mac, never on the host. The caller must drive the session (tokiwa_claim) and the MCP server must run with --actor. The agent sees a first line that says the message comes from an agent, not from the owner. The text is at most 16384 characters, with no control character except newline and tab, and does not start with /, ! or #. The result has turn_before: pass it to tokiwa_agent_wait as after.

tool.name: tokiwa_agent_answer
tool.description: Answer the pending single-select question of the agent of one Tokiwa session by choosing option choice (1 to 9). Take pending from tokiwa_agent_read with pending. A permission request has no answer: use tokiwa_interrupt to refuse it. The agent is told that an agent chose the answer, not the owner. The caller must drive the session and the MCP server must run with --actor.

tool.name: tokiwa_claim
tool.description: Become the driver of one Tokiwa session, the one actor that may send to it. The actor is the --actor of the MCP server. The call is refused while a client that can type is attached, and while another actor drives.

tool.name: tokiwa_release
tool.description: Give up the driver of one Tokiwa session. Only the driver can.

tool.name: tokiwa_end
tool.description: End one Tokiwa session and the programs in its panes. The call is refused while a client is attached. Take name and identity from tokiwa_sessions.

tool.name: tokiwa_cp
tool.description: Copy one file or one directory between this Mac and the Tokiwa host, in either direction, and return JSON with path, kind, files, bytes and sha256. One side is an absolute path on this Mac; the other is SESSION:PATH, relative to the folder of a session from tokiwa_sessions, or host:/PATH. On the host a copy reads and writes only the workbench folder and the session cache. An existing target stays unless force replaces a file; a directory is never replaced. At most 10 GB and 10,000 entries; a large copy can take minutes.

tool.name: tokiwa_commands
tool.description: List the commands that the owner allows on the host: each entry's name, description and argument shapes.

tool.name: tokiwa_run
tool.description: Run one entry of the owner's command list on the host and return its state and the first page of output as JSON. Take the entry and the argument shapes from tokiwa_commands. The host waits up to 8 seconds for the run to end; a run that is not done by then returns an id for tokiwa_run_status.

tool.name: tokiwa_run_status
tool.description: Read the state of a run and one page of its output as JSON, from a byte offset. Use next_offset from the last result to read on.
